judge_assessment.explanation: Every mathematical claim the judge made checks out against the artifacts. worksheet.tex plots A(2,5), B(6,3), C(4,8), D(9,1), E(0,6), F(7,7); the key's C = (4,8) and D = (9,1) match the TikZ coordinates exactly, PQ = 8-3 = 5, RS = 9-2 = 7, C is 8-3 = 5 higher than B, the two-rules table gives y = 2x with y(3)=6, y(4)=8 and next pair (5,10), and the reading log 3,5,4,8,5 sums to 25 with mean 5. Problem 10 is correctly typed `manual` and its desc names what full credit needs. But 'manual_items_reviewed: 1' understates what this sheet actually asks a human to judge, and the judge did not compare printed response slots against verify entries. worksheet.tex prints 37 \ansblank plus 12 \underline{\hspace{...}} response slots -- 49 in all -- against 15 verify entries. The clearest miss is problem 2: it prints 'C = ( __ , __ )' and 'D = ( __ , __ )' for extra practice, the answer key supplies C = (4,8) and D = (9,1), and verify.json holds nothing at all for those four blanks. Six further prompts ask for an explanation or a name ('Which arrow is E sitting on?', 'Why did you not need the y-coordinates?', 'Which coordinate is the same for both points?', 'Does that change how much higher C is?', 'Does the new point sit on the same straight line?', 'Which week was Maya's best?') and four problems ask the student to PLOT points, none of which is recorded as manual.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 3 puts E at (0,6) -- on the y-axis -- and the answer key spends a paragraph on it: 'Children often feel a coordinate of 0 must be a mistake, because you didn't do anything. Zero is a real instruction: it says do not go across.' A zero coordinate is exactly the case a first-quadrant sheet usually omits, and it is placed at difficulty 2 where it can still be taught rather than punished.

The same six-point grid is redrawn inside problems 1, 2, 3 and 6 rather than referenced once at the top, so a Grade 4 reader never has to hold a picture from a previous page in memory. Problems 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 each carry their own empty grid for plotting, which is why check_layout's figure-scope rule is satisfied without a value-free reference figure.

Problem 6's declared trap is the real error: subtracting the x-coordinates (4 - 6 = -2) when asked how much HIGHER C is than B. The key turns it into a physical check -- put a finger on each point and slide both straight down; the vertical gap never changes -- rather than restating the rule.

root_causes.description: The gate requires one check per problem id, so a problem may print any number of further blanks unchecked. On this sheet 49 printed response slots are backed by 15 verify entries, and several of the uncovered slots are final answers the key prints, not intermediate steps.
evidence: worksheet.tex lines 95-96 print C = ( __ , __ ) and D = ( __ , __ ); verify.json id 2 holds only B's x=6 and y=3
answer_key.pdf p1 supplies 'C = (4, 8) and D = (9, 1)' -- answers with no machine check behind them
worksheet.tex line 230 prints three \ansblank table cells for Rule B (4, 6, 8) and line 251 a 'two times' blank; verify.json id 7 holds only y(3)=6 and y(4)=8
worksheet.tex lines 269-273 print the next x (5) and the pair (5,10); verify.json id 8 holds one entry, 2*5 = 10
worksheet.tex line 301 prints five weekly readings (3,5,4,8,5); verify.json id 9 checks only their sum 25 and mean 5

root_causes.description: Explanation prompts and drawn work are recorded as if the neighbouring numeric entry covered them. Only problem 10 is typed `manual`, though six other problems end in a written-answer rule and four ask the student to plot and label points.
evidence: worksheet.tex line 131 'Which arrow is E sitting on?', line 155 'Why did you not need the y-coordinates to answer that?', line 179 'Which coordinate is the same for both points?', line 216 'Does that change how much higher C is?', line 276 'Does the new point sit on the same straight line as the others?', line 307 'Which week was Maya's best?' -- each followed by an \underline rule
Problems 4, 5, 7 and 8 instruct 'Plot ... label them ... join them with a straight line'; verify.json records only the derived arithmetic (5, 7, 6/8, 10)
verify.json has exactly one `manual` entry, id 10
final_response.md: 'Problem 10 is flagged for manual review' -- the delivery message inherits the same undercount

improvements.title: Count verification coverage per printed blank, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the sheet-side gate so coverage is counted per printed response slot, not per problem id. tests/check_answer_line.py already segments the worksheet and reads verify.json; have it also count the response slots each segment prints (\ansblank, \answerline, \ansline, and \underline{\hspace{...}}) and fail when a problem prints more slots than its id has verify entries, unless the surplus is explicitly absorbed by a 'manual' entry. SKILL.md's JSON-format section should state the rule as 'one check per printed blank', replacing today's 'at least one check per problem id'.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_unit_binding.py gains a fixture built from problem 2 of this case: a segment printing 'Across \ansblank Up \ansblank', 'B = ( \ansblank , \ansblank )', 'C = ( __ , __ )' and 'D = ( __ , __ )' with a verify.json holding only the two B read_data entries. Assert check_answer_line.py exits 1 naming problem 2 and the four uncovered slots; add read_data entries for C and D and assert exit 0. The gate has no slot count today, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The four coordinates the key already prints for C and D become machine-proved, and the same rule closes the table cells in problem 7, the next pair in problem 8 and the five readings in problem 9. Suite-wide this is the dominant finding (61 cases), so the gate is the cheapest place to fix it once.
improvements.risk: Slot counting is lexical, so a decorative rule (a 'name:' line, a worked-example blank inside the directions) could be counted as an answer slot and force a spurious entry. Restrict the count to slots inside a \problem segment and allow a `slots` override in the JSON for the rare deliberate case.

improvements.title: Flag the six written prompts and four plotting tasks as manual review
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual-coverage gate to the build chain. A new checker (tests/check_manual_coverage.py, wired into scripts/build.sh beside answer-line-ws) segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.py and, for each problem, scans the printed prose for open-response cues -- 'Explain', 'Why did/does', 'Say why', 'What went wrong', 'describe', 'in one or two sentences', 'Which ... did/was' followed by a rule blank, and the drawing verbs 'Plot', 'Shade', 'Draw', 'label' -- and requires the matching id in verify.json to carry at least one entry of type 'manual'. Exit 1 with the offending sentence quoted when it does not. SKILL.md line 257 already states the rule ('Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer'); nothing enforces it, and per-problem coverage (SKILL.md line 189) is satisfied by any single machine entry on the same id.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_manual_coverage.py adds a fixture from problem 4 of this case: 'Plot P(3,6) and Q(8,6), label them, and join them with a straight line ... Why did you not need the y-coordinates to answer that?' with a verify.json holding only eval q-p = 5. Assert the checker exits 1 for both the drawing verb and the 'Why' prompt, and exits 0 once a manual entry is added for id 4. The fixture passes every current gate, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The delivered count of manual items rises from 1 to the number the sheet actually contains, so a parent grading this packet is told which answers a machine proved and which they must read. It also makes the prompt's 'clearly label any genuinely open response' auditable.
improvements.risk: Over-flagging turns a machine_first sheet into a manual pile and would annoy users who wanted an auto-gradable worksheet. Mitigate by requiring the cue to precede a response slot and by reporting manual items as exit 2 (green with manual review), which the build chain already distinguishes from failure.

case_summary: A genuinely good Grade 4-5 coordinate packet -- every plotted point, distance, pattern pair and statistic recomputed here and correct; the answer key teaches rather than answers (the zero-coordinate paragraph on problem 3 and the 'watch the child's finger' note on ordered pairs are the best writing in this batch); the study guide is two pages with rule, example and try-it per skill. The ACCEPT stands. What the judge did not test is verification coverage: 49 printed response slots against 15 verify entries. Problem 2's C and D ordered pairs are answered in the key and checked nowhere; problem 7's three table cells, problem 8's next x and ordered pair, and problem 9's five weekly readings are in the same position. Six written prompts and four plotting instructions are also unflagged, while only problem 10 carries `manual`. Nothing here is wrong on the page -- it is unproved, which is a different and quieter risk.
